title: Radiation reaction as a singular model reduction

items.title: The nonrelativistic Abraham–Lorentz equation as a restricted effective model

references.title: Fritz Rohrlich, The Dynamics of a Charged Particle, arXiv:0804.4614 (complete 11-page full-text paper)
references.locator: Sections 1–2, PDF pp. 2–6: the finite-size/slow-force restriction, the nonrelativistic third-order equation, and its first-order reduction. The Gaussian-unit coefficient is converted to the stated SI convention; the paper's broader 'physically correct' conclusions are not adopted.

references.title: Jack Vanderlinde, Classical Electromagnetic Theory, Fundamental Theories of Physics, Springer (2004), complete 426-page book PDF
references.locator: Chapter 12, §§12.2–12.4, printed pp. 333–339 (PDF pp. 340–346): the energy-balance and rigid-sphere routes to the Abraham–Lorentz coefficient, the mass-renormalized effective equation, and the runaway/future-boundary branches. The text explicitly notes that its rigid extended sphere is inconsistent with special relativity; its derivation is not used as the proof of the postulate.

items.physical_scope: An additional restricted nonrelativistic effective model for a point particle represented by one trajectory in a named laboratory chart, driven by a prescribed external force. The equation is adopted rather than derived from the Maxwell self-field or the external Lorentz-coupling postulate. Its physical interpretation is limited to intervals and force profiles explicitly declared to be low-speed and slowly varying; this item sets no universal empirical cutoff and reports no experiment.

items.title: Runaway and bounded-future branches of the Abraham–Lorentz equation

references.title: Fritz Rohrlich, The Dynamics of a Charged Particle, arXiv:0804.4614 (complete 11-page full-text paper)
references.locator: Sections 1–2, PDF pp. 2–6: the nonrelativistic Abraham–Lorentz equation and discussion of its runaway and pre-acceleration branches. The complete branch classification and bounded-future proof here are local.

references.title: Jack Vanderlinde, Classical Electromagnetic Theory, Fundamental Theories of Physics, Springer (2004), complete 426-page book PDF
references.locator: Chapter 12, §12.4, printed pp. 338–339 (PDF pp. 345–346), equations (12–38)–(12–41): the homogeneous exponential runaway and the future-weighted solution selected by a future boundary condition. The item independently proves the exact ODE statement for every bounded continuous force.

items.physical_scope: Exact conditional properties of the adopted nonrelativistic prescribed-force ODE for bounded continuous forces: every acceleration solution, the unique solution bounded on a future half-line, and an explicit smooth future force for which that selected branch accelerates before the force begins. The proof concerns the formal effective equation only; it asserts no measured preacceleration, no self-consistent Maxwell–Lorentz trajectory, and no empirical validity outside the stated model regime.

items.title: First-order reduction of order with an explicit residual and error bound

references.title: Fritz Rohrlich, The Dynamics of a Charged Particle, arXiv:0804.4614 (complete 11-page full-text paper)
references.locator: Section 2, PDF pp. 4–6, equations (3a), (5a) and the first-order-in-$\tau_0$ discussion: the nonrelativistic reduction-of-order form and its slow-force restriction. The exact residual and uniform bound here are proved locally.

references.title: Jack Vanderlinde, Classical Electromagnetic Theory, Fundamental Theories of Physics, Springer (2004), complete 426-page book PDF
references.locator: Chapter 12, §§12.3–12.4, printed pp. 335–339 (PDF pp. 342–346): the Abraham–Lorentz coefficient, the mass-renormalized ODE, and its future-boundary solution. The item independently proves an explicit second-derivative error bound for the prescribed-force model.

items.physical_scope: Exact residual and an absolute acceleration-error bound for the first-order reduction of order of the adopted prescribed-force ODE, on the unique bounded-future branch and for bounded twice continuously differentiable forces with bounded second derivative. The result is conditional on the effective model; it is not a bound for nonlinear self-consistent Maxwell–Lorentz trajectories, and it gives no experimental validation.

title: Radiation reaction as a singular model reduction — Examples

items.title: Zero force leaves an exponentially growing acceleration branch

references.title: Fritz Rohrlich, The Dynamics of a Charged Particle, arXiv:0804.4614 (complete 11-page full-text paper)
references.locator: Section 1, PDF pp. 2–3: the runaway solution of the nonrelativistic Abraham–Lorentz equation.

references.title: Jack Vanderlinde, Classical Electromagnetic Theory, Fundamental Theories of Physics, Springer (2004), complete 426-page book PDF
references.locator: Chapter 12, §12.4, printed pp. 338–339 (PDF pp. 345–346), equation (12–38) and the homogeneous solutions.

items.physical_scope: A constructed mathematical example in the adopted Abraham–Lorentz ODE: zero prescribed force admits an exponentially growing acceleration branch, and position plus velocity at one time do not select it. This is a model property, not an observed particle trajectory or an empirical claim.

items.title: Harmonic forcing gives an exact error criterion for reduction of order

references.title: Fritz Rohrlich, The Dynamics of a Charged Particle, arXiv:0804.4614 (complete 11-page full-text paper)
references.locator: Section 2, PDF pp. 4–6, equations (1)–(2) and (5a): the small-$\tau_0$ and slowly varying-force context for first-order reduction.

references.title: Jack Vanderlinde, Classical Electromagnetic Theory, Fundamental Theories of Physics, Springer (2004), complete 426-page book PDF
references.locator: Chapter 12, §12.4 and problem 12-2, printed pp. 338–342 (PDF pp. 345–349): the future-weighted branch and a harmonic-oscillator application. The exact response and tolerance criterion here are calculated locally.

items.physical_scope: An exact harmonic-forcing calculation for the adopted prescribed-force ODE. It quantifies the model's absolute phasor-amplitude error for first-order reduction of order and shows that a fixed small tolerance requires small $|\omega\tau|$. It is not an empirical frequency-response measurement or a validation of a self-consistent radiation-reaction law.
